issues.failure_explanation: The one-sided pointwise bound is false for sign-changing factors: for the admissible case α = 2 with f = cos x_1, g = −cos x_1 the right-hand side is identically zero while (−Δ)(fg) = −2cos(2x_1), which is positive on a set of positive measure. Moreover an L^2 norm bound cannot follow from a one-sided pointwise inequality carrying no absolute value on the left, so the 'Consequently' step is an invalid inference. The whole proof is a one-line deferral asserting an adaptation of a cited lemma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Discard the pointwise claim and prove a valid L^2 fractional Leibniz (Kato–Ponce type) estimate of the stated consequence's form with an appropriate constant; only that consequence is used downstream.
issues.overall_effect: The nonlinear estimate (est_nonl) in Lemma conv_lemma, and with it the uniform H^{1+α} bound, the compactness convergence argument, and the error analysis of Theorem thm:spectral_accuracy, lose their justification as written.
issues.title: False pointwise product inequality for the fractional Laplacian
issues.why_classification: Replacing the lemma by a standard but nontrivial Leibniz-type estimate preserves every claim and rate, but requires more than a local edit.
